clue.text: Needle person breaking end off ruler

indicators.note: taking the end off a word means its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: BOD is informal British slang for a person
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Someone snaps the tip off a ruler and uses it as a makeshift needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' reads as the action in the surface but only joins the two parts. BOD is everyday British slang for a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin is a blunt, thick needle with a large eye, used for threading tape or elastic.

clue.text: Patience, say, of Aberdare politician somewhat used up

indicators.note: somewhat means only some of the words, a part tucked inside them
in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A Welsh politician's patience has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: Patience is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, not the virtue; 'say' marks it as an example. Aberdare is a Welsh town.
explanation.definitionFit: Patience is one of the Gilbert and Sullivan stage works, an example of the musical-drama form.

clue.text: Tease sweetheart about grand spent originally for leather items

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier words wrap round this letter
originally points to the first letter of the word, where it begins

blocks.note: to kid is to tease
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds
love as a term of endearment
the opening letter of spent

explanation.surface: Teasing a sweetheart over a thousand pounds splashed out on leather goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' wraps the tease and sweetheart words round the grand, so the G lands between them. A grand is slang for a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid gloves are made of soft leather from young goatskin, so they are leather items.

clue.text: Stylish new number, except for intro

indicators.note: an intro is the opening, so the first letter is left off

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
fifty is a number

explanation.surface: A fashionable new song, apart from its opening bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a song, but it is a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Nifty is informal for smart, neat and stylish.

clue.text: Secluded track from spa unknown tramp ultimately blocks

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter only of the following word
something that blocks sits inside a passage, so these letters go into the middle of the other word

blocks.note: Bath is the English spa town
Y is an algebraic unknown
the final letter of tramp

explanation.surface: A hiker leaves the spa town by a quiet path, its end blocked by a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: Y and P together go inside BATH, splitting it after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A bypath is a little-used side path, away from the main road, hence secluded.

clue.text: Kind of soup that Robin might make?

definitions.text: Kind of soup that Robin might make?

blocks.note: surface reading: a variety of soup, a Chinese delicacy
setter's reading: Robin as a bird, building a home in spring

explanation.walkthrough: The capital R makes Robin look like a cook's name; it is the bird, building its home.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird's-nest soup is a Chinese delicacy made from swiftlet saliva nests; a robin builds such a structure.

clue.text: Assume, for sake of argument, foreign banker's appeal

blocks.note: the Po is an Italian river, a 'banker' as it has banks; 's included
IT is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A foreign financier makes a plea, assuming something hypothetically.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' is a crossword term for a river, which has banks; the foreign one here is Italy's Po.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward a premise as the basis for reasoning.

clue.text: Actor, great in ad being broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A performer is superb in a commercial being shown on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles.

clue.text: Stay cold south of that French Canadian region

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of means placed below, so these come after

blocks.note: que is French for that
to be is to remain or stay
C is the abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: Stay somewhere chilly below that French-speaking part of Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French Canadian' looks like one unit but splits: French belongs with 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quebec is a province of eastern Canada, a large region of the country.

clue.text: About right time to become customer

blocks.note: C is short for circa, about
a lien is a legal right over property
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Around the proper moment, a visitor becomes a paying shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is not R here but a lien, a legal claim to hold someone's goods until a debt is paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is someone who buys services from a professional, a customer.

clue.text: Greatly alter parking during university term

indicators.note: during places one thing in the middle of the time span of another, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
U is the standard abbreviation for university
a term can mean an end or limit

explanation.surface: Parking arrangements are overhauled during the university term.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside U plus END, landing between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, figuratively to change it drastically.

clue.text: Anticipate everyone will back team from Nottingham

indicators.note: to back something is to stand behind it, so this part comes after the other

blocks.note: Nottingham Forest is the city's football club
synonym

explanation.surface: A football fan predicts that the whole crowd will support the Nottingham side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like supporting the team, but it means coming behind it. Nottingham Forest is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to act in advance to prevent something, so it means to anticipate and pre-empt.

clue.text: Apple tree Harry regularly recalled in past

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, every other one
recalled means called back, so the letters are taken in the backward direction
in places these letters inside the surrounding word

blocks.note: past and by both mean going beyond, as in walking past or by
an elm is a tree
the second and fourth letters of Harry

explanation.surface: Harry fondly remembers the apple tree from years gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: The tree and the picked letters of Harry are reversed as one unit before going inside the word for past.
explanation.definitionFit: Bramley is a large green English cooking apple variety, so it is an example of an apple.

clue.text: Drunk in this place gives defiant retort

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
synonym

explanation.surface: A drunk in the pub snaps back a defiant reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as an adjective, but it is the noun, a person who drinks too much.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So there!' is a childish exclamation of defiance ending an argument, a classic retort.

clue.text: Volcanic islands with deep cave meandering river enters

indicators.note: meandering means winding about aimlessly, so the letters are rearranged
entering means going inside, so this letter is placed within the rearranged ones

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A volcanic island with a deep cave through which a winding river runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meandering' seems to describe the river, but it acts on the words before it; R then goes inside, after the second E.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Verde is an Atlantic archipelago nation off West Africa formed by volcanic activity.

clue.text: Long to secure gold trophy for prickly individual

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so one word holds the others

blocks.note: to pine is to long for
or is the heraldic word for gold
a cup is a trophy

explanation.surface: A prickly character yearns to win the gold trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is the verb, to yearn. Or is the heraldic term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A porcupine is a rodent covered with sharp quills, literally prickly; the phrase also hints at a touchy person.

clue.text: Concerning bill, one unexpectedly rising

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so the letters fall into an unforeseen order

blocks.note: re means concerning or about
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A proposed law causes one politician to stand up unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like getting to one's feet, but it means an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising is a revolt against authority, the same as a rebellion.

clue.text: Change work period

blocks.note: first meaning: to move or alter
second meaning: a stint of work, as in a night stint at a factory

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single phrase about altering working hours, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for moving or altering and a noun for a scheduled stint of labour.

clue.text: Number working were almost set to accept bribe

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
working means being worked on or kneaded, so the letters are reshaped
to accept means to take in, so the other letters hold this word inside

blocks.note: ten is a number
taken as written
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: A number of workers were nearly ready to take a backhander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like describing the number of workers, but it scrambles the words after it; 'almost' trims only the second of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is slang for a bribe or inducement offered to sway someone.

clue.text: Smears philosopher in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is judged by its spoken sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: Karl Marx, the German philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher's speech is full of smears against opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smears' looks like slander but is meant as stains or blotches.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks and smears are both stains or blemishes left on a surface; here the plural noun or verb.

clue.text: Flipping con involving American women's colourful fliers

indicators.note: flipping turns something over, so the letters run backwards
involving means wrapping in, so one word encloses the others

blocks.note: a scam is a con
A is the abbreviation for American
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A wretched swindle drawing in American women's bright aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' is also a mild British expletive, which is how it reads in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaws are large brightly coloured parrots, so they are vivid flying birds.

clue.text: Brownish-grey goat crackpot chases

indicators.note: something that chases comes behind what it pursues, so this part follows

blocks.note: a butter is something that butts, as a goat does
a nut is an eccentric or crazy person

explanation.surface: A lunatic runs after a goat, a grey-brown one.
explanation.walkthrough: A goat is a 'butter' in the cryptic sense of one that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Butternut is a colour named after the dyed homespun cloth, a brownish-grey shade.

clue.text: Undertake challenge

blocks.note: first meaning: to take on a task
second meaning: to confront someone, or to try to take the ball from an opponent

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like accepting a dare; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both starting work on a problem and confronting or challenging someone directly.

clue.text: Uncle, so desperate to get advice

indicators.note: desperate suggests wild and out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nephew asks his uncle for advice, so anxious is he.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel is a formal word for advice or guidance given to someone.

clue.text: Situation understood, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is identified by what is heard, its sound

blocks.note: seen in the sense of understood, as in 'I see'

explanation.surface: Someone reports that the state of affairs has been grasped.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is a setting or state of affairs, as in the political scene.

clue.text: Meeting Conservative, Rita is agitated and abusive

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up and shaken, so the letters are mixed up
meeting means coming up against, so the two parts are placed side by side

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Rita meets a Tory politician, gets worked up and starts hurling insults.
explanation.walkthrough: C follows the rearranged letters even though Conservative comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Satiric writing mocks and ridicules its targets, so it can be bitingly abusive.

clue.text: That girl kept avoiding outsiders, those wearing fleeces?

indicators.note: avoiding the outsiders means leaving off the outer letters, keeping only the inner ones

blocks.note: she refers to a girl
the middle letters of kept

explanation.surface: A girl keeps clear of strangers, like fleece-clad hikers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleeces' suggests outdoor jackets; the question mark signals the woolly coat of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep grow fleeces of wool, so they are the ones literally wearing them.

clue.text: Merrymaking in bar over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are read the other way

blocks.note: a lever is a bar used for prising

explanation.surface: Partying away in the pub until the night is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like the pub but is a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: Revel can be a noun for lively festivity, the same as merrymaking.

clue.text: Spooner's healthy booze one serves just before this

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so initial sounds are exchanged

blocks.note: light wine, low in calories, is the healthy drink; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: A drinker offers a healthy tipple just before serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serves' looks like pouring drinks, but it is a tennis serve, taken from behind the baseline.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the server stands just behind the white baseline marking the court's end.

clue.text: Book hotel, ignoring photos essentially

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core, the middle letters of the word
ignoring means leaving something out, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: Novotel is an international hotel chain
the two central letters of photos

explanation.surface: Reserving a hotel room without looking at the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The hotel is a specific one, Novotel, a chain found across Europe; remove its central OT.
explanation.definitionFit: A novel is a long work of fiction, a type of book.

clue.text: Cleric describes this writer as humble

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw a line around, so one word encircles the other

blocks.note: a dean is a senior cleric
the setter referring to themself

explanation.surface: A churchman describes the writer as a modest person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describes' in the sense of tracing a circle round something; 'humble' is the verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, which is to humble or humiliate them.

clue.text: Stout or wine lady's content to leave

indicators.note: the contents, the inside letters, are gone, so only the outer pair is kept

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
the first and last letters of lady

explanation.surface: At the bar: stout or wine? The lady is happy to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer, alongside wine, but it is the adjective; 'content' is the noun meaning what is inside, not the adjective meaning happy.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly describes a person who is stout, plump and round-bodied.
